data.title: Comstock Announces Grand Opening of Ebbitt House at Reston Station
data.description:
First-ever expansion of D.C.’s iconic Old Ebbitt Grill opens its doors at 1860 Reston Row Plaza in The Row at Reston Station

RESTON, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Comstock Holding Companies, Inc. ( CHCI ) (“Comstock”), a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments, today announced the grand opening of Ebbitt House at Reston Station. Located at 1860 Reston Row Plaza in The Row at Reston Station, the 12,000-square-foot restaurant opens its doors to the public today at 11 a.m. and will welcome guests daily. Reservations are now open via EbbittHouse.com and OpenTable.

Named after the original 1856 boarding house that gave rise to the legendary Old Ebbitt Grill, Ebbitt House marks the first-ever expansion of the storied brand outside of downtown D.C. in its 170-year history. Designed as a contemporary evolution of the D.C. landmark, the venue brings the signature Clyde’s Restaurant Group (“CRG”) hospitality, classic American fare, lively bar culture, and renowned raw bar to Northern Virginia’s premier mixed-use, transit-oriented neighborhood.

Ebbitt House features more than 400 seats spread across its 275+ guest dining room, two private dining rooms, and all-season patio. Two indoor bars anchor the main dining areas that are complemented by a dedicated outdoor patio bar. A full oyster and raw bar sits at the heart of the restaurant, carrying forward one of Old Ebbitt Grill’s best-known traditions, alongside a menu of elevated American classics that have drawn generations of guests to the original. Located steps from the Wiehle-Reston East Station on Metro's Silver Line, Ebbitt House is positioned as a destination for business lunches, after-work gatherings, and celebratory events alike.

“Ebbitt House is one of the most anticipated restaurant openings in Northern Virginia's history, and we are proud that CRG chose Reston Station for the first-ever expansion of such an iconic brand,” said Tim Steffan, Chief Operating Officer of Comstock. “Its arrival, alongside the JW Marriott Reston Station and our growing roster of best-in-class dining and retail, further cements Reston Station as the premier place to live, work, stay, and gather in the Dulles Corridor.”

The opening of Ebbitt House in Reston Station also marks CRG’s return to the area. CRG previously operated Clyde’s of Reston at Reston Town Center for more than 30 years, and several familiar faces from that team have rejoined to lead Ebbitt House, including General Manager Ajay Bhatia and Executive Chef Diego Ramirez.

"Reston has always held a special place in our history, and we are thrilled to return to this thriving community with a bold new chapter of the Ebbitt story," said John McDonnell, President and CEO of Clyde’s Restaurant Group. "Ebbitt House honors and expands upon the traditions guests love about Old Ebbitt Grill, from our renowned raw bar to our classic American hospitality, while introducing an elevated menu and an energetic, modern space tailored specifically for Reston Station."

Reston Station is among the largest and most prominent mixed-use, transit-oriented developments in the Mid-Atlantic region, covering approximately 90 acres spanning across the Dulles Toll Road and surrounding the Wiehle-Reston East Station on Metro’s Silver Line. Its first two phases feature five Trophy-Class office buildings, two luxury high-rise apartment towers, and Virginia’s first and only JW Marriott – a 28-story tower that includes the world-class JW Marriott Reston Station hotel and the ultra-premium JW Marriott Residences, both of which set the new standard for luxury in the D.C. region. A growing collection of signature dining, retail, and wellness options include Ebbitt House, Founding Farmers, Davio’s Northern Italian Steakhouse, Starbucks, a 55,000-square-foot VIDA Fitness and Spa, CVS, and more. For more information, please visit RestonStation.com.

About Comstock

Comstock is a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments. With over four decades of industry expertise, Comstock’s vertically integrated operating platform delivers long-term value across a rapidly growing portfolio of premier properties that includes two of the most prominent mixed-use, transit-oriented developments in the Mid-Atlantic region. Leveraging its scalable, asset-light, debt-free business model, Comstock has strategically expanded into large-scale AI and digital infrastructure development and established an active position in one of the real estate industry's top-performing segments. For more information, please visit Comstock.com.

data.title: Samuel Automation Expands U.S. Presence with Acquisition of Alpha Integration
data.description:
WATERLOO, ON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Samuel Automation, an integrator of modern automation solutions and a division of Samuel, Son & Co., Limited, has acquired Alpha Integration. The acquisition strengthens Samuel Automation's U.S. network, adding regional scale and complementary expertise in custom automated assembly, inspection and material handling solutions.

Based in Nashville, Tennessee, Alpha Integration is a trusted provider of custom automated assembly and inspection equipment, recognized for its engineering expertise, quality solutions and customer-focused approach. The company serves customers in a diverse range of industries, including automotive, cosmetics, electrical, construction and life sciences.

"Alpha Integration's outstanding team and deep automation expertise make this acquisition a natural fit," said Simon Drexler, President, Samuel Automation. "By bringing our teams and capabilities together as one network, we can combine local customer support with broader expertise and scalable project execution. Nashville also gives us an important U.S. base from which to serve customers and grow."

"Joining Samuel Automation gives us the scale, resources and complementary expertise to accelerate innovation, create new opportunities for our employees and deliver even greater value to our customers," stated Matt Phillips, President, Alpha Integration.

Effective immediately, Alpha Integration will operate as Samuel Automation – Nashville, becoming an important part of Samuel Automation's growing North American network.

About Samuel Automation

Samuel Automation is an automation and technology solutions provider that combines systems integration, specialized engineering and technology capabilities, and lifecycle support to help manufacturers improve and scale their operations. Through its North American network, Samuel Automation brings together regional execution capacity and specialized expertise to solve complex manufacturing challenges. For more information visit SamuelAutomation.com.

About Samuel

Founded in 1855, Samuel, Son & Co., Limited, is a family-owned integrated network of metal manufacturing, processing and distribution divisions. Samuel employees provide metals, industrial products and related value-added services from locations across North America. The company leverages its industry expertise, breadth of experience and the passion of its people to help drive success for North American business – one customer at a time. For more information visit Samuel.com.

data.title: Sagtec Global Limited Announces Additional Share Acquisition by CEO, Reinforcing Confidence in Long-Term Growth Strategy
data.description:
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sagtec Global Limited ( SAGT ) ("Sagtec" or the "Company"), a provider of AI-powered software solutions and enterprise technology platforms, today announced that its Chief Executive Officer and major shareholder, Mr. Ng Chen Lok, has acquired an additional 260,000 Class A ordinary shares of the Company from an existing shareholder through a privately negotiated transaction at a purchase price of US$1.03 per share, representing an aggregate purchase consideration of US$267,800.

The latest acquisition follows Mr. Ng's previous purchase of 300,000 Class A ordinary shares in July 2026, further demonstrating his continued personal investment in the Company and confidence in Sagtec's long-term growth strategy.

CEO Strengthens Ownership and Voting Position

Following the acquisition, Mr. Ng's beneficial ownership of Class A ordinary shares increased from 8,752,600 shares to 9,012,600 shares. Mr. Ng also continues to hold 2,000,000 Class B ordinary shares, representing 100% of the Company's outstanding Class B ordinary shares. Under Sagtec's dual-class share structure, each Class A ordinary share carries one vote, while each Class B ordinary share carries twenty votes. As a result, the acquisition brings Mr. Ng's total beneficial ownership to 11,012,600 ordinary shares across both classes.

Continued Commitment to Sagtec's Growth Strategy

The additional investment comes as Sagtec continues to advance its strategic initiatives in artificial intelligence, enterprise software, and digital infrastructure, with a focus on strengthening its technology capabilities and expanding its presence in international markets.

Sagtec remains committed to developing innovative AI-powered solutions, expanding its product portfolio, and pursuing strategic business opportunities designed to support sustainable revenue growth and long-term shareholder value creation.

Mr. Ng Chen Lok, Chief Executive Officer of Sagtec Global Limited ( SAGT ), commented:

"Our continued investment in Sagtec reflects our strong belief in the Company's long-term potential and the opportunities ahead. We have established a solid foundation for growth, and we remain confident in our ability to execute our strategic vision as we expand our AI-powered solutions and strengthen our position in the technology sector.

"As both Chief Executive Officer and a major shareholder, I remain personally committed to Sagtec's future. This additional investment reflects my confidence in our business strategy, our team's execution capabilities, and our ability to build sustainable long-term value for shareholders."

About Sagtec Global Limited ( SAGT )

Sagtec Global Limited ( SAGT ) is a Malaysia-headquartered AI technology company providing AI-assisted software solutions, enterprise technology platforms, and digital transformation services to businesses across Southeast Asia. The Company develops customizable enterprise software, intelligent data management platforms, and cloud-based technologies that support digital transformation across multiple industries. Its proprietary solutions, including the Speed+ cloud-based smart ordering platform, currently serve more than 12,000 clients. Since its IPO in March 2025, Sagtec has expanded its operations across Malaysia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. For more information, visit www.sagtec-global.com.

These statements include, but are not limited to, statements regarding the Company's future business prospects, growth strategy, market opportunities, strategic initiatives, and shareholder value creation. data.title: Phunware Files Definitive Proxy Statement and Issues Letter to Stockholders
data.description:
Board of Directors Cite Progress on and Acceleration of 2.0 Strategy

Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 Supported by Strong Leadership Team,
Balance Sheet and Liquidity

Company Urges Stockholders to Vote “FOR” Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE Proxy Card

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phunware, Inc. ( PHUN ) (“Phunware” or the “Company”) , a mobile-first AI-enabled guest intelligence platform company focusing on hotels, resorts, health systems and other large complex properties, has filed its definitive proxy statement and today issued a letter from its Board of Directors (the “Board”) to stockholders ahead of the Company’s 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders (the “Annual Meeting”), which will be held virtually on December 17, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time.

The letter outlines the recommendation of the Board’s Special Committee on Election Matters for stockholders to re-elect Board Chairperson Elliot Han for another term as a Class II director, the Company's progress and prospects under its 2.0 Strategy, and its responses to the proxy materials filed by Goldenwise Capital Group Limited (“Goldenwise”). Shareholders of record as of October 19, 2026, are entitled to vote at the Annual Meeting.

What You Need to Know Before You Vote.

At the December 17, 2026 Annual Meeting, stockholders will vote on a nominee to fill one Board seat. The Special Committee urges you to vote “FOR” Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card.

  • Mr. Han has played a key role in strengthening Phunware’s finances and leadership. He championed the approximately $104 million capital raise in 2024 that resolved liquidity challenges. As of September 30, 2026, Phunware ( PHUN ) held approximately $86.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, with no debt. Further, as Chairperson, led the appointment of Dmitry Kroshka as permanent CEO, ending a period of interim leadership.
  • Goldenwise has not made a convincing case. It has not made any proposals establishing how replacing Mr. Han would improve Phunware’s new strategy, customer acquisition, product commercialization, recurring revenue growth or other critical performance metrics. Stockholders deserve a clear explanation of how Goldenwise’s nominee would improve the Company and its prospects.
  • Mr. Ding’s disclosure record raises serious questions. He answered “No” when asked whether he had been involved in any prior proceedings involving allegations of a breach of fiduciary duty or similar conduct, despite being named in a 2020 lawsuit alleging professional negligence and breach of fiduciary duty involving approximately $1.3 million in alleged investment losses. Separately, Goldenwise only provided more fullsome public disclosure of its short call and short put options after Phunware ( PHUN ) questioned the accuracy and completeness of these disclosures. Shareholders deserve complete and accurate information from Goldenwise as they are being asked to vote in favor of its nominee for the Board.
  • Ms. Zhang’s commercial ties and track record warrant scrutiny. Her firm, Trunity Partners, had a business relationship with Goldenwise in 2025, and she served alongside Mr. Ding on Moberg Pharma’s board for just under eight months, where she was not re-elected in May 2026. Her independence from Goldenwise and what relevant experience she would bring to Phunware’s Board deserve scrutiny.
  • An independent review concluded Mr. Han is the stronger choice. A Special Committee of independent directors, with Mr. Han recused, evaluated both candidates. He brings a wealth of relevant public-market leadership experience, capital-markets and finance expertise, legal training, governance experience as Audit Committee chair and audit committee financial expert, and a hands-on role shaping and implementing the Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 Strategy. Ms. Zhang’s background is not additive to the Board’s aggregate skillset. Mr. Han’s extensive knowledge of Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 supports continuity as the Company works to convert its investments into signed customer agreements and recurring revenues.

How to Vote

Vote FOR Elliot Han only, on the WHITE proxy card, by Internet, telephone or mail, by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 16, 2026. Discard any GOLD card: a later-dated GOLD card cancels your WHITE vote. Questions? Call Alliance Advisors toll-free at 1-888-244-0487.

Letter to Stockholders

Dear Stockholders:

We believe Phunware ( PHUN ) is at a critical point in its evolution and transition. The Phunware Board and management team have been strengthened, a new vision and strategy referred to as “Phunware 2.0” is now being implemented, and the related hospitality and healthcare intelligence platforms, modules and products are in development. We are very focused on finalizing and adopting our 2027 operating plan and budget for Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 and completing and converting our 2.0 Strategy into revenues and enterprise value for our stockholders. We believe that continuity and uninterrupted execution at the top are very important to completing the 2.0 Strategy and ensuring those investments turn into growth for stockholders.

At Phunware’s 2026 Annual Meeting on December 17, 2026, stockholders will elect one Class II director to a three-year term. The Board’s nominee is Chairperson Elliot Han. Goldenwise Capital Group Limited, a Hong Kong-based investment manager led by its founder Mr. Huakun Richard Ding, has put forward Ms. Xuan Zhang in opposition to Mr. Han.

Stockholders should carefully examine the record, relationships, and objectives of anyone seeking Board influence. Mr. Ding began engaging with Phunware ( PHUN ) only this year. Against that limited history (and as discussed in more detail below), the discrepancy in his signed director questionnaire, Ms. Zhang’s commercial ties to Goldenwise and Mr. Ding, and the absence of a specific operating plan or alternative strategy presented by Mr. Ding warrant heightened scrutiny before stockholders entrust his nominee with a seat on the Board. In our view, Goldenwise has been far more specific about the Board influence it wants than the value its nominee would create for Phunware ( PHUN ) and its stockholders.

The question is not whether Ms. Zhang has useful qualifications: the question is whether replacing Mr. Han would make the Board stronger and improve Phunware ( PHUN ) and its prospects. The Board’s Special Committee on Election Matters concluded it would not, by concluding, among other items, that:

Mr. Han has delivered. He championed a capital raising strategy that resolved near-term liquidity challenges in 2024; he led the Board’s appointment of a permanent CEO, ending a period of interim leadership, paired with the installment of fuller executive bench; and he strongly supported and provided oversight and guidance on a near daily basis for implementation of our new Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 Strategy. Mr. Han went above and beyond to use his first term to lay a strong foundation for future growth, and his renomination ensures the Board can build on it without disruption.

Goldenwise has offered no plan. Despite repeated Board invitations to do so, Goldenwise failed to present any other specific operating plan or alternative strategy for Phunware ( PHUN ). Goldenwise now appears to support the 2.0 Strategy, and require an operating plan and budget, with spending requirements and dated milestones - all of which the Board intends to do for 2027.

The Special Committee recommends that you vote FOR Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card.

Why the Special Committee Recommends Elliot Han

Mr. Han has served on the Board as an independent director since January 2024 and as Chairperson since October 2025. He also chairs the Audit Committee and is designated an audit committee financial expert. His experience includes senior roles at Cantor Fitzgerald, the New York Stock Exchange, and Goldman Sachs, in addition to practicing corporate law at Freshfields. He is currently the Chief Investment Officer of C1 Fund Inc., a publicly traded closed-end investment fund, and a Partner at PGP Capital Advisors.

For stockholders, we believe the most important qualifications for a director at Phunware ( PHUN ) are:

  • Direct knowledge of Phunware’s business, technology, and 2.0 Strategy to challenge and support management and evaluate execution.
  • Financial and transactional expertise to oversee funding decisions, capital allocation, and inorganic growth.
  • Governance and leadership experience to support effective oversight and transparency as the Company moves forward.

As a Board member, Mr. Han advocated for and facilitated Phunware’s completion and utilization of its 2024 at-the-market equity financing program, through which the Company raised approximately $104 million. This capital addressed significant near-term liquidity needs and materially strengthened Phunware’s balance sheet and reduced debt, providing Phunware ( PHUN ) with the financial flexibility to pursue a strategic reset, adapt to macro headwinds, invest in strategy and product development, and evaluate inorganic growth opportunities. Since the commencement of his Board chairmanship in October 2025, Mr. Han helped develop and advance the Company's strategic pivot to Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0, pushing Phunware ( PHUN ) from a legacy wayfinding and enterprise mobile development company to the AI-powered Guest Intelligence Platform phase and enabling execution of the strategy by helping appoint Dmitry Kroshka as permanent CEO and assembling an experienced product, marketing, sales, and finance team of employees and senior advisors to implement Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0. He sharpened the Company’s focus and promoted operating discipline around defined platforms and related modules, products and customer propositions.

Importantly, Mr. Han’s contributions to the Board and the Company extend beyond financing and strategy. He has chaired the Compensation Committee, during which time he helped oversee CEO succession and disciplined executive and employee incentives, including conserving capital and aligning leadership incentives with the Company’s turnaround and performance. He has chaired the Audit Committee, during which he oversaw financial reporting, external audits, compliance, and risk controls. He has also led the Strategic Transactions Committee’s oversight of potential acquisitions and capital deployment. Mr. Han demonstrated leadership during a transformational turnaround period, navigating the Company through organizational changes and overseeing the Company’s responses to litigation matters while limiting management distraction. His level of commitment has been demonstrated through his attendance at all Board and committee meetings, substantive travel, preparation, participation, and substantial availability for Company matters.

To ensure an independent evaluation of the director candidates, the Board established a Special Committee on Election Matters, composed of independent directors Quyen Du and Ed Lu; Mr. Han was recused from such deliberations. After weighing the qualifications and fit of all candidates, the Board’s collective capabilities, and the Company’s current and foreseeable needs, the Special Committee determined that Mr. Han’s demonstrated contributions, independent judgment, and unique combination of capital markets, technology investments, legal, corporate finance, and transactional expertise, together with his governance and leadership experience and deep knowledge of Phunware ( PHUN ) and the 2.0 Strategy, made him the clear best choice. Continuity alone does not entitle a director to re-election, but it is extremely valuable at present because of Mr. Han’s specific experience, institutional knowledge of Phunware’s business, operating and management history, demonstrated leadership through periods of market and organizational transitions, oversight, and complementary fit as Chairperson and a member of the Board.

Why Replacing Mr. Han with Goldenwise’s Nominee Would Not Benefit Stockholders

The Special Committee is aware of Ms. Zhang’s qualifications and experience in investment management, capital allocation, and strategic advisory work. However, the materials provided and reviewed did not establish a sustained record of experience which the Board is focused on, including direct responsibility for commercial scaling, go-to-market experience, deep domain knowledge in hospitality and healthcare, AI, platform launches, executive management and operating leadership, and post-acquisition integration experience. In light of the Company’s needs and existing Board composition, these were and are important considerations for new directors as Phunware ( PHUN ) moves its AI-powered Guest Intelligence Platform and other components of Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 towards commercialization.

Ms. Zhang’s known public-company board experience consisted principally of approximately eight months on the board of Moberg Pharma, a company listed in Sweden. Although proposed for re-election, Ms. Zhang did not retain her seat at Moberg’s May 21, 2026 annual meeting, when stockholders elected an alternative slate that excluded her. Ms. Zhang's director questionnaire described her experience with investment and oversight frameworks, but the Committee did not find and Goldenwise has not shown sufficiently specific support for the proposition that her background and experience would improve Phunware’s product-market fit, technology expertise, commercialization milestones, or decisions about potential operating decisions or strategic alternatives. Also, her disclosed biography does not identify service on the board of a U.S.-listed company, and Goldenwise has not shown how her experience would strengthen the Board’s existing expertise in U.S. public-company governance and financing or in Phunware’s business.

The question for stockholders is not whether Ms. Zhang possesses useful professional qualifications. It is whether replacing Mr. Han with Ms. Zhang would strengthen the Board or improve the Company or its prospects, in particular the Company’s implementation of its 2.0 Strategy. The Committee concluded that her investment expertise and advisory background did not establish a sufficiently differentiated contribution in key areas of interest to the Board to offset the loss of Mr. Han’s demonstrated capital-markets, corporate legal, transaction, governance, and Phunware ( PHUN )-specific experience or meet the anticipated operational needs in the Company’s next phase in the 2.0 Strategy. As such, the Committee supported and recommended Mr. Han’s renomination.

Progress Under Phunware’s 2.0 Strategy

Since February 2025, two new independent directors joined the Board: Quyen Du, formerly Head of Corporate Strategy and Development of Condé Nast, and Ed Lu, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer of Fandom. In May 2026, under Mr. Han’s Chairmanship, the Board appointed Dmitry Kroshka as Chief Executive Officer, ending a period of interim CEO leadership and establishing a clear direction for the Company's 2.0 Strategy.

Under the 2.0 Strategy, Phunware ( PHUN ) is bringing together its mobile, location-aware, and customer-engagement capabilities with AI to develop a shared intelligence platform for hospitality, healthcare, and other complex property verticals. We are excited about Phunware’s prospects under the 2.0 Strategy and believe it will be very beneficial to building long-term value for stockholders. Please see our stockholder letter released in October 2026, which can be accessed here, and our investor deck also posted in October 2026, which can be accessed here, for more information and detail on our 2.0 Strategy and recent milestones.

We have ample liquidity to implement and execute our 2.0 Strategy, including through inorganic growth opportunities. As of September 30, 2026, Phunware ( PHUN ) held approximately $86.7 million in cash and cash equivalents with no debt.

Your Board and management team remain focused on disciplined technology and data development, product sales and revenues, capital allocation and inorganic growth opportunities, demonstrating commercial progress, and keeping stockholders informed as we execute the 2.0 Strategy.

Goldenwise Has Not Presented a Specific Operating Plan or Alternative Strategy

We welcome stockholder input and recognize that every investor has the right to question our performance, strategy, and governance. However, a request for Board representation should be supported by a clear explanation of what would change and how stockholders would benefit.

Goldenwise has not proposed a specific operating plan or alternative strategy for Phunware’s business or growth or explained how its nominee would improve Phunware ( PHUN ) or its execution of the 2.0 Strategy. The Goldenwise materials provided so far are long on criticism and short on constructive substance. The Company invited Mr. Ding, on multiple occasions, to present specific proposals on product, strategy, acquisitions, capital allocation, and stockholder communications. To date, he has failed to present any such proposals. This is consistent with the pattern Goldenwise has shown throughout: demand Board representation, focus on broad generic themes that Phunware ( PHUN ) is already addressing, fail to engage on substance and details, and then accuse the Company of stonewalling.

Goldenwise’s demands for Board representation have shifted considerably. In April 2026, Mr. Ding urged the Board to add two or three directors. In June 2026, he proposed expanding the Board from three (3) to six (6) members and subsequently submitted four potential candidates, including himself. Goldenwise is now seeking to have one nominee elected to fill the single available seat. The number of seats sought has changed, but the demand for Board influence, without a specific operating plan or alternative strategy, reflects, in our view, an unfocused and undeveloped proposal. Stockholders should expect a clear, focused and developed plan and greater conviction from someone seeking to reshape the Board. As noted above, there is no need to reshape the Board to implement Phunware ( PHUN ) 2.0 with appropriate operating plan and budget: that will occur, and we welcome shareholder input on implementation of the adopted plan.

On broad themes and engagement, Goldenwise’s own proxy materials document discussions with the Company’s legal team on April 14, 2026, and meetings with the Board on May 15 and June 30, 2026, regarding those themes. The Company also prepared and offered to enter into a confidentiality agreement with Goldenwise and Mr. Ding to enable deeper discussions that could involve nonpublic information. Goldenwise’s proxy states that Mr. Ding declined on June 5, because the agreement might restrict further stock purchases or otherwise disadvantage stockholders. Confidentiality agreements of this kind are customary when an investor seeks access to nonpublic information. They protect all stockholders by ensuring that no single investor has access to information that other investors do not have when making trading decisions. Goldenwise’s later disclosures of short call and short put positions alongside its shareholdings reinforced, in the Company’s view, the importance of those protections. If Goldenwise and Mr. Ding signed the agreement, the Company believes the parties would have had a fuller and more meaningful dialogue.

Stockholders Deserve a Full and Accurate Context

Goldenwise’s criticisms of director compensation and leadership changes omit important details and context.

The August 2026 equity awards Goldenwise cites were granted under Phunware’s Outside Director Compensation Policy, which was adopted by the Board under a prior Chairperson who is no longer on the Board in June 2024 and benchmarked to market practice, well before Goldenwise began accumulating its reported position. The policy provides for non-discretionary annual director restricted stock unit awards with a stated value of $150,000. Goldenwise also mischaracterizes these awards by suggesting that these awards for Board service are discretionary, which they are not, and that these awards should have had an acquisition cost, which would be extremely uncommon and inconsistent with market practice.

Board compensation is also now paid in arrears rather than in advance for quarterly board services rendered, which further aligns directors with stockholders. Given Phunware’s internal resource challenges and the critical issues that it has been facing, Mr. Han and the other directors have consistently committed more time than is customary throughout their respective Board tenures.

On leadership changes, two of the three CEO transitions Goldenwise highlights occurred before Mr. Han became Chairperson in October 2025. The last two interim CEOs were appointed under the leadership of the above referenced prior Chairperson. The most recent CEO transition was the Board’s appointment of Dmitry Kroshka as permanent Chief Executive Officer in May 2026, under the leadership of Mr. Han as Chairperson, ending the interim leadership period. These distinctions matter when assessing the current Board leadership.

The Committee Also Considered Ms. Zhang’s Ties to Mr. Ding

The Special Committee considered Ms. Zhang’s professional and business relationships with Mr. Ding, including their overlapping service on the Moberg Pharma board and a sub-advisory arrangement between Ms. Zhang’s firm, Trunity Partners, and Goldenwise during 2025. These relationships require scrutiny when assessing whether she would as a Board member exercise judgment independently of the investor sponsoring her candidacy. Calling a nominee independent does not make her commercial ties to that investor irrelevant.

Mr. Ding’s record at Moberg Pharma also warrants scrutiny. Between August 13 and October 5, 2026, while remaining a director, he reported sales totaling 988,607 Moberg shares. Phunware ( PHUN ) stockholders should not confuse a demand for Board influence with a commitment to remain invested for the long term. By contrast, no current Phunware ( PHUN ) director has sold Phunware ( PHUN ) shares during his or her Board tenure (other than to cover taxes upon vesting of shares).

Goldenwise Demands Transparency While Its Own Record Raises Serious Questions

Goldenwise has called for greater transparency from the Board option positions, while its own disclosures to the Company leave serious gaps. In 2020 a complaint was filed in federal court naming Mr. Ding and Goldenwise Capital Management, Inc. as defendants, alleging professional negligence and breach of fiduciary duty arising from approximately $1.3 million in alleged investment losses over several days. This complaint is a matter of public record. Yet Mr. Ding submitted a signed director questionnaire to the Board (at a time when he was proposing himself and three (3) others for Board seats) answering “No” to a direct question asking whether, during the prior 10 years, he had been the subject of a legal proceeding involving breach of fiduciary duty, gross negligence, or similar conduct. In the Company’s view, this discrepancy raises questions about the completeness and accuracy of information provided to the Company in connection with the Goldenwise nominations. A demand for transparency by Goldenwise carries little weight without full candor from the person making it.

The disclosure concerns extend beyond the lawsuit. Mr. Ding’s signed questionnaire identified short call and short put options but provided insufficient detail to understand their terms and economic effect. Goldenwise’s July 10 and July 14 public filings did not describe those positions. Phunware ( PHUN ) publicly questioned these gaps on July 16. Four days later, Goldenwise added contract counts, strike prices, and expiration dates to its filing. Shareholders deserve an explanation for why fuller disclosure followed a public challenge from the Company. These positions also matter when assessing Mr. Ding’s claim of complete alignment with shareholders. Goldenwise’s October 20 filing disclosed short call options alongside long shares and short puts. Short calls can limit participation in a share price recovery above the strike price, while short puts can increase exposure to further declines. These arrangements can create different risks and rewards from those of shareholders who simply hold the stock. Before accepting Mr. Ding’s claim of complete alignment, shareholders deserve a full understanding of the financial interests behind his campaign.

Goldenwise May Seek Reimbursement for Its Campaign

Goldenwise estimates its solicitation costs at approximately $130,000 and stated that, if successful, it intends to seek reimbursement from Phunware ( PHUN ), without submitting such reimbursement to a stockholder vote. Its campaign to reduce Company spending therefore comes with a potential bill for its own expenses.

Stockholders Have Significant Reason to be Cautious

data.description:
Starting at just $25 per month, Kelt Forge helps entrepreneurs and small businesses turn ideas into websites, web apps and mobile applications without traditional programming.

MISSION VIEJO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kelt Agentic Systems, LLC today announced the launch of Kelt Forge, an AI-powered software creation platform designed to help individuals and businesses build the technology they imagine. Starting at just $25 per month, the platform offers a new way to create, refine and expand software using everyday language.

Instead of starting with a development team or learning to code, users describe what they want to build. Kelt Forge helps generate the software, provides tools to make changes, and offers interactive previews so users can see their ideas take shape. The platform supports business websites, web applications, and iOS and Android mobile projects.

Turning Imagination Into Reality

For small businesses, the challenge is often not a lack of ideas but the cost and complexity of bringing them to life. A company might need a customer portal, a quoting system, an internal operations dashboard or a mobile experience tailored to how its team actually works. Off-the-shelf software may require businesses to change their processes; traditional custom development can put more ambitious ideas out of reach.

Kelt Forge is built around a different approach: describe a need, create a working starting point and continue improving it as the business evolves. Users can return to a project, request new features, review changes and move toward publishing from the same workspace. The goal is to make software creation an ongoing capability.

Founder Ken Eynon drew on his experience building and improving software for Sivility Systems, including websites, accounting-related workflows and sales tools. That experience shaped his belief that business owners should be able to create technology around their operations instead of forcing their operations to fit someone else's software.

"For $25 a month, you're not just investing in software. You're investing in the freedom to keep creating," said Eynon.

Kelt Forge combines AI-assisted development, project iteration and platform-specific preview and publishing workflows in one environment. Mobile app distribution remains subject to the applicable Apple and Google developer-account requirements and approvals.

Kelt Forge is designed for entrepreneurs, small-business owners and creators who want to turn practical ideas into useful digital products, from stronger online experiences to custom operational tools.

Learn more at www.kelt.com.

data.title: Fed's Paulson backs further rate hikes, says shared understanding beats guidance
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in a speech delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson said after her formal remarks that the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high in an otherwise robust economy.

"I see growth that's strengthened and I see a labor market being at full employment, and so it's clear that inflation needs to be ... the priority" of monetary policymaking right now, Paulson said after her formal remarks.

"The way we bring inflation down is by having higher rates," she said, adding that there is "more tightening to do."

Paulson also said that slow and steady rate rises rather than dramatic action give the economy time to adjust to the increase in short-term borrowing costs.

Paulson holds a vote on the FOMC this year. The committee, which sets interest rates, is widely expected to raise its target rate of between 3.75% and 4% at the meeting scheduled for December 8-9.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October, after boosting them in September while signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said.

"A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis and Tom Hogue)

data.title: Soccer-Eckert signs new deal as Southampton manager till 2029 despite 'spygate' controversy
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Southampton coach Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract through 2029, the second-tier club said on Friday, despite uncertainty over his future following his role in the "spygate" scandal.

Eckert was handed a suspended six-week ban and fined £28,000 ($36,697) after admitting he authorised the observation of training sessions involving three rival Championship clubs last season.

The Football Association charged Eckert in July, with an independent regulatory commission imposing the sanctions after a hearing. The governing body confirmed in October that the ban would remain suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season.

"We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment we have had for the last 12 months," Eckert told the club website.

"I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come."

Eckert guided Southampton from 21st place to a fourth-placed finish last season. However, the club were thrown out of the Championship playoff final and docked four points for the 2026-27 campaign over the "spygate" affair.

Southampton, who are seventh in the Championship standings, host Derby County on Saturday.

($1 = 0.7630 pounds)

data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq futures slide as Anthropic retreat deepens AI jitters
data.description:
* Futures down: Dow 0.1%, S&P 500 0.74%, Nasdaq 1.64%

* Anthropic down 7.4% a day after debut

* Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nov 20 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures fell more than 1% on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 7.4% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings this week were seen as key tests of whether battered investor confidence in the AI trade could recover.

But neither revived enthusiasm after weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

As of Thursday's close, the Nasdaq was 13.6% below its October 6 record closing high, while the S&P 500 had posted its sixth consecutive loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) declined more than 1.5% each, while Meta fell 2% and Alphabet was muted. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 2.2%, while Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Marvell ( MRVL ), and Micron lost between 2.2% and 6.6%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped about 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN ( IREN ), Applied Digital ( APLD ) and Core Scientific ( CORZ ) fell about 4% each.

At 7:03 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 48 points, or 0.1%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 53.5 points, or 0.74%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 436 points, or 1.64%.

The CBOE Volatility Index, Wall Street's fear gauge, hit the 30-point mark for the first time since March 30.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% beat analyst earnings expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 9.7% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

(Reporting by Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

data.title: Analysis-Trump touts Asia trade deal wins, but US agricultural exports disappoint
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump visited Asia this week, boasting of a string of agricultural trade victories since threatening to impose tariffs that would decimate other countries' trade.

US trade agreements have at times buoyed prices of crops and livestock, but a Reuters analysis of 10 deals showed few have generated a promised windfall of US farm product sales.

China, the largest US trading partner in Asia, appears on track to meet its commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans in 2026, but purchases remain below levels seen before Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs in April 2025. Beijing's agreement to buy $17 billion worth of other US farm products this year is largely unfulfilled.

The data undercuts White House messaging that Trump's trade tactics are benefiting US farmers and ushering in what the president has called a "golden age" of agriculture. Dissatisfaction over the president's tariff strategy contributed to losses for Trump's Republican Party in this month's midterm elections, including among farmers who voted for Trump, analysts say.

The Trump administration says it has secured around a dozen trade deals with Asian countries since imposing tariffs, easing plant and livestock health requirements for incoming US products and expanding low-tariff import quotas. Some included minimum annual purchase commitments for US crops and meat.

But agricultural exports to partner nations often increased immediately following White House announcements before tapering off, the Reuters analysis found.

"The reality is that this has been a lot of talk and not much action," said Scott Lincicome, vice president of economics and trade at the Cato Institute think tank.

During Trump's Asia trip this week, he said the US reached a "very big trade deal" with the Philippines. Manila said, however, the two countries had reached an understanding on economic cooperation.

MISSED TARGETS

Some deals have been finalized, but have not met their targets.

Indonesia, the 12th-largest US agricultural products importer by value, agreed in February to import $4.5 billion of farm goods. But in the first nine months of 2026, US exports totaled less than $2.4 billion, roughly in line with the same period over the last decade, according to US Census Bureau trade data.

Indonesia agreed to import 3.5 million tons of US soybeans annually, but just 54% of that goal had shipped as of September, the trade data showed. Wheat exports of less than 450,000 tons represented less than a quarter of Indonesia's annual commitment, while soymeal exports of just 150,000 tons made up 4% of a 3.8-million-ton target.

The White House said a trade agreement with Malaysia, signed in October 2025, would provide US exporters "unprecedented access" to its market. The deal promised to open market access for US sorghum and facilitate pork and poultry exports. However, 2026 US pork exports through September were down 52% from the same period a year earlier, while there were zero poultry and sorghum shipments, US government data showed.

The text of a February trade deal with Bangladesh, following Trump's threat of tariffs that could devastate the South Asian nation's textiles industry, stated that the country or companies there would buy at least 700,000 tons of US wheat annually for five years and $1.25 billion worth or 2.6 million tons of soy and soy products over one year. Since then, US wheat exports totaled 473,000 tons while combined soybean and soymeal shipments reached just 162,000 tons, US government data showed.

Trade talks with China have shown mixed results. Trump met on Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen after a brief stop in the Philippines for a Southeast Asian summit.

The world's top soybean importer halted purchases from the US last year as the trade war heated up, but resumed modest purchases after talks in Busan, South Korea, last October and in Beijing in May. But China has not lifted its 10% tariff on US soybeans, so government buyers booked the nearly 20 million tons from the current US harvest. Private Chinese importers continued to buy from rival supplier Brazil.

The White House said it secured a deal for Beijing to buy $17 billion of other US agricultural goods annually, with this year's target prorated. But the US has exported less than $2.5 billion of US farm goods, excluding soybeans, to China since the May summit through September, US government data showed.

In a statement, the White House said China has achieved "partial compliance" with its Busan agreement, but did not respond to detailed questions about other Asian trading partners. The Office of the US Trade Representative did not have immediate comment.

Trump's trade approach has damaged the country's reputation as a reliable trading partner, according to analysts and exporters, and spurred traditional trading partners to strike deals with rival exporters.

"Everybody else in the world is like, 'We are not going to follow Trump off the tariff cliff. We're not going to really retaliate against the United States, but we'll retaliate indirectly by lowering our barriers to everybody else'," Lincicome said.

(Reporting by Karl Plume in Chicago. Editing by Emily Schmall and Rod Nickel)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks slide as AI selloff deepens, Asia has worst week since 2020
data.description:
* Asian stocks on track for worst week since COVID hit

* Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade

* US futures fall after S&P 500 drops for six straight sessions

(Updates prices, adds comment and chart)

By Harry Robertson, Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

LONDON/HONG KONG/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector, with US futures dropping and Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020.

Government bonds rallied as investors sought safe-haven assets.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, jumped as it launched the biggest IPO in history on Thursday, although they pared gains later in the session and were down 10% in premarket trading on Friday.

The debut did little to revive excitement over the broader AI theme, however, as investors continued to question whether the huge amounts of spending would deliver returns.

"The Anthropic IPO gave us some brief respite from the cloud of negativity," said Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar. "That pause is well and truly over unfortunately."

Futures for the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 fell 2% after the index dropped the same amount on Thursday. The Nasdaq is now down around 15% since hitting a record high in early October.

S&P 500 futures were in the red after the index fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday. A seven-day run of declines would be the worst streak since the pandemic.

The STOXX 600 gauge of European stocks fell almost 2%, while MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session , its longest losing streak since 2023.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan tumbled and has sunk 8% this week, its worst performance since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blowout earnings earlier in the week and Anthropic's IPO have both failed to restore confidence, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at bank and investment firm Saxo.

"The market is no longer looking for proof of AI demand alone," she said. "It wants evidence that the extraordinary spending across the ecosystem can generate sustainable returns."

The VIX index of expected volatility on Wall Street stocks jumped and traded at its highest since March on Friday.

Adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

"No one headline drove the roll, though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment," said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

All of that has piled further pressure on the AI trade, already battered in recent weeks by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia ( NVDA ) and growing anti-data-centre sentiment exemplified by the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5%. Taiwanese shares were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990.

Despite the sharp drop in stocks, however, equity markets remain up for the year after a blistering rally in the first half on AI optimism.

TREASURIES RALLY AS INVESTORS TAKE COVER

US Treasuries rallied as stocks took a beating, sending investors towards assets deemed safe havens.

The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes fell for a fifth straight session, to below 5%, while German 10-year bond yields fell 10 bps, the most since April . Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Meanwhile, the US dollar held steady at around its highest level in 20 months, also garnering support from growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in.

Oil prices were steady, with Brent crude futures trading at $90 a barrel and on track for a third week of declines.

(Reporting by Harry Robertson in London, Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Lincoln Feast, Xevi Fontdegloria and Mark Potter)

data.title: Consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R and PPF Completes Acquisition of InPost
data.description:
• InPost completes its transition to private ownership, backed by a Consortium committed to accelerating its growth as a leading European consumer-centric e-commerce enabler.
  • InPost remains operationally independent and headquartered in Poland, led by CEO and founder Rafał Brzoska and the existing management team.
  • Advent, FedEx ( FDX ), A&R and PPF bring together long-term capital, deep sector knowledge, complementary commercial expertise and broad industry networks to help drive InPost’s future growth across Europe.
  • The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s pan-European out-of-home network, underpinned by continued innovation in its technology platform and consumer proposition.
  • InPost’s growth strategy will be supported by arm’s length commercial agreements connecting InPost’s B2C last-mile capabilities to FedEx’s global network of c.3 million businesses and 225 million recipients.
  • The transaction will seek to deliver tangible benefits across InPost’s growing network, from stronger delivery infrastructure for merchants and greater convenience for consumers across Poland and Western Europe to continued career growth opportunities for employees.

AMSTERDAM & LUXEMBOURG--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates (“Advent”), FCWB LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of FedEx Corporation ( FDX ) (“FedEx”), A&R Investments Ltd. (“A&R”) and PPF Group (“PPF”), together forming the Consortium, today announce the completion of the acquisition of InPost S.A. (“InPost” or the “Company”). InPost is now wholly-owned by the Consortium and has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam.

A new chapter for InPost

Completion of the acquisition marks a significant milestone for InPost, a leading European out-of-home e-commerce enablement platform. The business will continue to operate as a standalone, operationally independent company under its existing brand, with its headquarters, management structure and innovation remaining in Poland. Founder Rafał Brzoska continues to lead the Company as CEO, and the executive leadership team which has underpinned InPost’s success to date remains in place, carrying forward the vision he set out when founding the business in 1999.

With an out-of-home network of over 100,000 locations, comprising more than 70,000 automated parcel lockers and close to 30,000 pick-up and drop-off points, the Consortium believes InPost has a clear path to extend its reach further. Backed by the Consortium’s capital, expertise, deep sector experience and shared vision, InPost will work to strengthen its position in Poland and expand across Europe, including in the UK, Italy, France, Spain, Portugal and the Benelux region. InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network.

At its core, InPost is a technology-driven business aiming to redefine the European e-commerce sector by improving the delivery experience for consumers and merchants alike. The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s digital offering and consumer experience, including its mobile app, as it innovates to increase its consumer appeal. Enabled by this technology platform and leading out-of-home network, the Consortium believes InPost is well-positioned to benefit from structural sector tailwinds, including increasing e-commerce penetration, rising consumer demand for speed and convenience, and the shift towards more sustainable delivery solutions.

To help deliver this growth, InPost and FedEx ( FDX ) are exploring separate commercial opportunities to provide FedEx ( FDX ) merchants access to InPost’s B2C capabilities while leveraging FedEx’s global network to support the Company’s growth. As an example, the two companies have entered into arm’s length commercial agreements enabling selected recipients the use of InPost’s last-mile capabilities and out-of-home infrastructure in Europe.

The partnership between the Consortium and InPost aims to deliver benefits for all InPost stakeholders. Employees will continue to be able to build their careers within a strengthened business, empowered by a fast-growing, innovative culture. Merchants can expect a more advanced, better-connected delivery network and continued investment in the technology that serves their consumers. And consumers across Poland and Western Europe will have the opportunity to experience greater convenience, more choice and a faster way to shop and receive goods – driven by InPost’s consumer-centric innovations and growing delivery network.

The Consortium believes its investment, collective sector knowledge and experience will support InPost in continuing to build a leading platform for parcel delivery and returns across Europe.

Rafał Brzoska, Founder and CEO of InPost, said: “This partnership delivers the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler. I’m proud of how far we have come since founding InPost in 1999 in Poland, growing into one of Europe’s largest delivery networks. We’re taking this step with partners who have known InPost for years and understand our business and ambitions. With the Consortium’s expertise and backing, we will accelerate our investment in the technology and consumer experience that set us apart, bringing them to even more consumers and merchants across Europe.”

Ranjan Sen, Managing Partner at Advent, said: “We began our journey with InPost and Rafał in 2017, when we invested in a promising local leader with the potential to become a European champion. InPost has since grown to over 100,000 locations across Poland and Western Europe, and we are proud to reiterate our conviction in Rafał and his team. Drawing on our successful track record of investing in both InPost and the wider logistics sector, we look forward to working alongside our Consortium partners to help drive the next stage of the Company’s growth.”

Raj Subramaniam, President and CEO of FedEx ( FDX ), said: “FedEx is the heartbeat of the global industrial economy, and InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment. Connecting our global network of 3 million businesses and 225 million recipients with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth. We see significant opportunity to expand our commercial arrangements across Europe and look forward to building on it as members of the Consortium.”

Didier Stoessel, Co-CEO of PPF, said: “When we first invested in InPost almost three years ago, we saw a strong business model with long-term growth potential as e-commerce and out-of-home delivery continue to expand across Europe. Our conviction in the Company has only strengthened since then. We are pleased to build on that relationship now by reinvesting alongside our Consortium partners and leveraging our knowledge of the Company as InPost enters this next chapter.”

Consortium structure

Following completion, the Consortium is structured with Advent holding 37%, FedEx ( FDX ) holding 37%, A&R holding 16% and PPF holding 10%. A&R has fully rolled-over its holdings in the Company and PPF has reinvested part of the proceeds from the tender of its existing stake to become a shareholder in the Consortium.

Notes to Editors:

About InPost

InPost has revolutionised e-commerce parcel delivery in Poland and is now one of the leading out-of-home e-commerce enablement platforms in Europe. Founded in 1999 by Rafał Brzoska, InPost provides delivery services through our network of more than 70,000 Automated Parcel Machines (“APMs”) across nine European countries, alongside courier and fulfilment services for e-commerce merchants. InPost’s locker network provides consumers with a cheaper, more flexible and convenient delivery option. Powered by in-house technology, InPost continuously develops and tests new services, from digital tools to e-commerce solutions, to make buying and selling online simpler for consumers and merchants.

Advent is a leading global private equity investor committed to working in partnership with management teams, entrepreneurs, and founders to help transform businesses. With 17 offices across five continents, we oversee more than USD $109 billion in assets under management* and have made 460 investments across 45 countries.

Since our founding in 1984, we have developed specialist market expertise across our five core sectors: business & financial services, consumer, healthcare, industrial, and technology. "Our base case for 2027 remains for economic growth close to trend, rising corporate profits, further growth in AI investment, and moderating inflation later in the year."

US large-cap funds attracted $31.7 billion during the week, their largest inflow in eight weeks. In contrast, mid-cap and small-cap funds recorded outflows of $1.15 billion and $535 million, respectively.

Among sectoral funds, technology funds attracted $10.3 billion, their largest inflow since June 16. Industrial and financial sector funds, meanwhile, saw notable outflows of $1.23 billion and $884 million, respectively.

US bond funds recorded their first weekly outflow in four weeks, with investors withdrawing a net $5.58 billion.

Long-term US government and Treasury funds and high-yield funds saw outflows of $2.64 billion and $2.31 billion, respectively. In contrast, short- to intermediate-term government and Treasury funds attracted $1.27 billion, while loan participation funds received $859 million.

data.title: Fujifilm Expands ECHELON Synergy 1.5T MRI with ZeroHelium Technology and Dockable Patient Table Option
data.description:
New ZeroHelium MRI with advanced imaging, automation and flexibility helps healthcare providers speed exams with enhanced image quality and efficiency.

LEXINGTON, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, a leading provider of diagnostic and enterprise imaging solutions, announces the latest evolution of its ECHELON Synergy 1.5T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) platform. The new release expands customer choice with the availability of ECHELON Synergy ZeroHelium system, designed to operate without liquid helium while delivering high-quality imaging, intelligent workflow and patient-focused design. Fujifilm will showcase the new system for the first time in the U.S. at booth #4100 in South Hall at the 2026 Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) Conference & Annual Meeting held November 29 to December 2.

With the latest version 11 upgrades, healthcare organizations can configure ECHELON Synergy according to their clinical, operational and facility needs, including the option to select a ZeroHelium or conventional magnet, as well as options with or without the SynergyGlide dockable patient table. SynergyGlide is a power-assisted dockable table to enable patient preparation and transport outside of the exam room, to streamline workflow, patient handling and comfort.

“Healthcare providers are looking for MRI technology that can address not only clinical performance, but the operational realities of running a modern imaging department,” said Henry (Hidetoshi) Izawa, President and Chief Executive Officer, Global Head of Medical Informatics, FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation. “With ECHELON Synergy version 11, we’re giving customers greater flexibility to configure an MRI solution to meet their clinical and operational needs. ZeroHelium adds an important new option by helping reduce infrastructure requirements, while the platform’s advanced imaging and automation technologies are designed to help technologists work efficiently and deliver a positive patient experience.”

MRI Without Liquid Helium

Superconducting MRI systems have historically relied on liquid helium to cool their magnet coils and maintain superconductivity. Fujifilm’s ZeroHelium technology uses a dedicated cooling system to maintain superconductivity at approximately -269°C without requiring liquid helium, eliminating dependence on liquid helium while maintaining MRI operation. It can also help reduce risks associated with helium loss during unexpected events or power interruptions and provide more predictable operating costs.

Designed with thermal and mechanical factors in mind, the ZeroHelium magnet uses advanced engineering to control thermal effects and suppress vibration within the magnet, helping maintain consistent image quality. When an emergency ramp-down is not required, in-house staff can ramp down and restart the magnet in just a couple of hours instead of days without requiring a liquid helium refill, helping simplify recovery and reduce potential downtime.

Designed to Advance Imaging Quality and Productivity

Beyond its magnet technology, ECHELON Synergy version 11 incorporates advanced imaging and workflow capabilities designed to improve MRI efficiency. The system’s Deep Learning Reconstruction (DLR) technology helps reduce noise and enhance image clarity and can be applied to all body regions and a wide range of sequences. IP-RAPID is designed to help shorten scan times, and DLR Plus is designed to further refine image quality.

Workflow capabilities, including AutoExam, AutoPose and Auto Series, are designed to help reduce repetitive manual steps throughout exam setup and scanning by automatically performing exam and positioning steps. In the U.S., AutoExam is available for knee exams only, and AutoPose is available for anatomical regions other than the brain. AutoPose provides automated positioning across multiple anatomical regions, while Auto Series helps streamline scan sequencing and exam workflow, allowing technologists to spend more time focused on the patient.

ECHELON Synergy Version 11, including the ZeroHelium configuration, also features Synergy Vision, with monitoring cameras positioned at the front and rear of the bore to help operators monitor patient movement. The technology can identify movements that may contribute to artifacts, such as coughing or sneezing. Separate post-processing capabilities are designed to help reduce motion artifacts and potential repeat scans.

Flexible Design Built Around Patients and Imaging Teams

ECHELON Synergy features a 70 cm wide bore and patient table designed for flexibility in positioning for a variety of patient sizes and examinations. Its adaptive coil portfolio includes FlexFit Neuro and flexible blanket coils designed to provide versatile anatomical coverage while enhancing patient comfort and high-quality imaging.

The ZeroHelium configuration can also improve operational efficiency beyond helium management. The system’s Smart Eco Plus functionality is designed to reduce energy consumption during idle periods, while Fujifilm’s remote monitoring and predictive diagnostics capabilities help identify potential issues early and enable proactive maintenance planning.

The ECHELON Synergy ZeroHelium MRI system with the SynergyGlide table was recognized with a 2026 Red Dot Product Design Award.

ECHELON Synergy ZeroHelium and ECHELON Synergy version 11 are available for sale in the United States. For more information about the system, visit here.

About Fujifilm

FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation is a comprehensive healthcare company that has an extensive range of technology and expertise in the detection, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases. Fujifilm’s innovative portfolio includes solutions spanning diagnostic imaging, enterprise imaging, endoscopic imaging, surgical imaging, and in-vitro diagnostics. The Non-Destructive Testing group delivers radiography solutions to ensure high accuracy inspection of transportation infrastructure, and assets within aerospace, and oil and gas industries.

The company is headquartered in Lexington, Massachusetts. For more information on healthcare offerings, please visit healthcaresolutions-us.fujifilm.com, and for NDT portfolio, please visit https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/business/industrial-materials/non-destructive-testing.

FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation, headquartered in Tokyo, leverages its depth of knowledge and proprietary core technologies to deliver innovative products and services across the globe through the four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging with over 70,000 employees. Guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles,” we address social challenges and create a positive impact on society through our products, services, and business operations. Under its medium-term management plan, VISION2030, which ends in FY2030, we aspire to continue our evolution into a company that creates value and smiles for various stakeholders as a collection of global leading businesses and achieve a global revenue of 4 trillion yen.
